Rebuild earlier colony snapshots from a pedigree's birth and exit dates

Source: R/backfillColonySnapshots.R
backfillColonySnapshots.Rd

Builds one Genetic-Health Trends snapshot for each past date from the birth and exit dates already in a pedigree, so a trend can be drawn without waiting seasons for recorded snapshots (issue #170). Each row is the same 27-column row createColonySnapshot makes and passes checkSnapshotHistory, filed under its own membership rule, "reconstructedLiving", so rebuilt rows form a line of their own and never mix with recorded ones.

Usage

backfillColonySnapshots(
  ped,
  dates = NULL,
  guIter,
  guThresh,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  by = "year",
  existingHistory = NULL,
  minAnimals = 2L,
  updateProgress = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

ped

A quality-controlled pedigree data.frame (see qcStudbook) holding at least id, sire, dam, sex, gen, birth and exit (the last two as Date columns), and a status column when the studbook has one. Pass the full pedigree, not one already trimmed to a focal list of animals.

dates

The dates to rebuild: Date values or ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) strings, at least one, with no missing or duplicated value. Leave it out (NULL) to build the series described by from, to and by; it cannot be combined with them.

guIter

Single positive whole number: the number of gene-drop iterations, recorded in each row. Required — there is no default, so the recorded settings cannot silently differ from the ones used.

guThresh

Single positive whole number: the genetic uniqueness threshold, recorded in each row. Required.

from

The first date of the series: a Date or an ISO-8601 string. The default is the first 1 January with at least minAnimals living animals.

to

The last date of the series, as from. The default is the last 1 January on or before the latest birth or exit date in ped.

by

The step of the series: a string for seq.Date, such as "year" (the default), "6 months" or "quarter".

existingHistory

A snapshot history to add to (see checkSnapshotHistory), or NULL for none. Its rows are kept as they are, with any extra columns, and a date whose "reconstructedLiving" row is already there is not rebuilt. A row of another membership rule on the same date does not count as already there.

minAnimals

Single whole number, at least 2 (the least reportGV can analyze): the fewest living animals a 1 January needs to start the default series. Default 2.

updateProgress

Function or NULL. If it is a function, it is called once for each date, after the date has been rebuilt, skipped or has failed, with the arguments n (the number of dates in the run), value (how many are done) and detail (the date as text), to update a shiny::Progress object. It is not passed on to reportGV.

...

Further arguments passed to reportGV (for example kinshipOverrides or twinRelations, the latter cut to each date as described above).

Value

A list of three data.frames. history: the rebuilt snapshots (and the rows of existingHistory, if given), in date order, in the 27-column snapshot-history schema. support: one row for each date in the run, with snapshotDate, nLiving (the animals counted), nPlacedByOffspring (of those, the ones with no birth date), nPossiblyAlive, pctSireKnown and pctDamKnown (the percentage of the living animals whose sire or dam is recorded, that is neither blank nor a generated stand-in; NA when nobody was alive). skipped: the dates not rebuilt, with snapshotDate and reason.

Details

The dates. Give dates, or leave it out for a series of by steps (one year by default) from from to to. Unless you give them, the series starts at the first 1 January with at least minAnimals living animals and ends at the last 1 January on or before the latest birth or exit date in the pedigree. minAnimals only moves that default start: a date you name, in dates or as from, is never refused for having few animals.

Who was alive. For each date the pedigree is copied and every exit date after that date is blanked, because the demographic effective-size estimators read the exit column as it stands (see calcNeSexRatio): without the blanking an animal that was alive on the date but has left since would not count as a living breeder. The population is the real animals alive on the date. An animal is alive from its birth date; one with no birth date is alive from the birth of its first offspring that has a date (it was born before that offspring). It is alive until its exit date. An animal with no exit date counts only when the studbook lists it as living, the test the application applies today (status ALIVE, or no exit date when the pedigree has no status column), so an animal whose status is UNKNOWN never counts. Generated stand-in parents never enter the population. The pedigree is trimmed to that population and its ancestors (trimPedigree), analyzed with reportGV, and summarized with createColonySnapshot. For the date a pedigree was exported, the row equals the snapshot the application records for that pedigree.

What each date rests on. The support table says how many animals were counted, how many of them were placed through an offspring, how many more the studbook does not rule out (animals with no birth date that are not counted and had not left), and how much of the parentage is recorded. No threshold refuses a date; read these figures beside the trend. Where few sires are recorded the sex-ratio effective size reads low because of the missing records, not because of the colony.

Dates that fail. A date that cannot be analyzed (for example one on which fewer than two animals were alive) does not stop the others. It is listed in skipped with the message of the error, and one warning says how many dates failed. When no date can be built, the function stops and names the dates. A date whose "reconstructedLiving" row is already in existingHistory is not rebuilt; it is listed in skipped without a warning.

Twin pairs. A twinRelations table (see checkTwinRelations) is used on each date as far as that date's animals allow. Declared identical ("MZ twin") animals form groups, as in kinship, so the pairs A-B and B-C make the group A, B and C. On a date the groups are cut to the animals in that date's pedigree, which holds the animals alive then and their ancestors; a group left with two or more animals is applied and the others are left out. An animal missing from the pedigree on a date cannot change anyone's kinship that day, so a twin born later, or one who left and has no descendants, no longer makes the date fail. An identifier that is in no pedigree at all is a mistake and stops the function before any date is built.

Limits: today's parentage and today's genotypes are used for every date, so a parent identified later is treated as known earlier; the effective sizes follow the definition of a living breeder in calcNeSexRatio; and two close dates can differ only by gene-drop sampling.

See also

createColonySnapshot, appendColonySnapshot, checkSnapshotHistory

Examples

ped <- nprcgenekeepr::qcPed
result <- backfillColonySnapshots(ped,
  dates = as.Date(c("2005-01-01", "2010-01-01")),
  guIter = 10L, guThresh = 1L
)
#> Warning: Founder genome equivalents undefined: founder(s) with positive contribution were retained in 0 of the gene-drop iterations; raise the number of iterations (K).
#> Warning: Founder genome equivalents undefined: founder(s) with positive contribution were retained in 0 of the gene-drop iterations; raise the number of iterations (K).
result$history[, c("snapshotDate", "membershipRule", "nAnimals")]
#>   snapshotDate      membershipRule nAnimals
#> 1   2005-01-01 reconstructedLiving       86
#> 2   2010-01-01 reconstructedLiving       63
result$support
#>   snapshotDate nLiving nPlacedByOffspring nPossiblyAlive pctSireKnown
#> 1   2005-01-01      86                  0              0     56.97674
#> 2   2010-01-01      63                  0              0     68.25397
#>   pctDamKnown
#> 1    89.53488
#> 2    90.47619

## a yearly series, added to the history above: the dates already there
## are not rebuilt
series <- backfillColonySnapshots(ped,
  from = "2005-01-01", to = "2008-01-01",
  guIter = 10L, guThresh = 1L, existingHistory = result$history
)
#> Warning: Founder genome equivalents undefined: founder(s) with positive contribution were retained in 0 of the gene-drop iterations; raise the number of iterations (K).
#> Warning: Founder genome equivalents undefined: founder(s) with positive contribution were retained in 0 of the gene-drop iterations; raise the number of iterations (K).
series$history[, c("snapshotDate", "nAnimals")]
#>   snapshotDate nAnimals
#> 1   2005-01-01       86
#> 2   2006-01-01       86
#> 3   2007-01-01       83
#> 4   2008-01-01       79
#> 5   2010-01-01       63
series$skipped
#>   snapshotDate                                                        reason
#> 1   2005-01-01 already in existingHistory under the reconstructedLiving rule
